findings.reason: naming `_running_jobs` as the single scheduler reader, or extending it, removes a fourth copy and ties §2's ledger check to the same owner.
findings.text: the plan has reload.py "find the profile's running serve job by job name" itself, but the repository already owns that query, and it is already copy-pasted three times: the owner is `_running_jobs` (imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:1219), the structured scheduler reader, while the duplicated profile-name filters live at imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:1117 (`shutdown`), imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:1994 (`key_command` rotate), and imas_ambix/agent/cli.py:2317 (`restart`); `_discover_live_routes` (cli.py:1446) reaches the same scheduler through `_running_jobs`. A fourth copy in reload.py is a fourth thing to keep in step when the scheduler output format or the account selector changes, and §2's capacity check ("`scontrol show node` AllocTRES for cards and memory, and the `gpu_0003_grpA` core ledger") re-derives per-job card/memory/node facts that `_running_jobs` already returns as `gres` and `node`.

findings.reason: naming `_probe_endpoint` as the readiness mechanism makes the plan's "generation validation is not an HTTP 200" point land on the existing probe instead of leaving readiness latent.
findings.text: `_probe_endpoint` already implements the `/v1/models` readiness probe (returning `probe.readiness == "ready"`) that the plan's "wait for readiness" step re-describes, and `_running_jobs` (cli.py:1219) already reports job `state`, which is the "wait for RUNNING" half; the plan names neither, so its readiness half is unspecified machinery beside an existing owner.

findings.reason: the section must account for the added CLI surface in its own text, which forces the author to decide whether `reload` and `restart` are one command with a mode or two.
findings.text: §1 adds `imas-ambix agent reload <slug>` with `--gpus`, `--cpus`, `--port`, `--no-speculative`, `--reason`, `--dspark-block-size`, `--time`, `--auth`, `--api-key`, `--dry-run`, and §2 adds `--mode auto|overlap|pause`, while `restart` keeps its identical option set; against this week's supplied counts (public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0) neither section states that `reload` supersedes, retires or merges any existing command or option, nor why the swap behaviour cannot be a mode of `restart`.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — one module, `imas_ambix/agent/reload.py`, hides the whole pause/drain/cancel/submit/rollback cycle behind a small injected interface, and §2 deliberately writes into the same module and command rather than a parallel one.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — the plan re-implements the profile-to-running-job scheduler lookup in `reload.py` rather than extending its owner, and the same lookup is already duplicated three times.
rubric_items.interface_budget: a finding — public_definitions 0, cli_options 0, mcp_views 0, refusal_families 0; §1 adds a new CLI command (`agent reload`) with `restart`'s full option set plus `--reason`, and §2 adds `--mode`, without either section naming what it retires or merges, or why nothing can be.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — the plan searches well for some mechanisms (it cites `_resolve_router_upstreams` cli.py:1507, `_preferred_owner` router.py:1639, `generate_serve_script` slurm.py:432, `classify_reading` lane.py:620, and `agent pause`) but adds its own readiness/validation wait without naming the `/v1/models` readiness probe that already exists.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: pass — the `reload` command is thin over the new `reload.py`, and the plan states it reuses `restart`'s profile resolution, port precedence and engine-environment check by name rather than copying them; it adds substantial behaviour (pause, bounded cycle, rollback) that no existing command carries.
